course_title: Resilience and Recovery in Tourism and Events
course_description:
This course examines a series of contemporary concepts and theories essential for understanding and responding to a range of global ethical issues that impact the tourism and events industries, particularly how these sectors respond and adapt to crisis and disasters. The course explores concepts such as ethics and social responsibility at the individual, organisational and destination levels.

This course introduces students to the concepts of resilience and recovery in the tourism and events industry. We live in a turbulent and ever-changing world and the tourism and events industry must prepare for, and respond to, many social and environmental issues and challenges. Some of these challenges are long-term stressors, such as climate change or global geopolitics, while other challenges come as a sudden shock - for example natural disasters or terrorist attacks. Students will be introduced to the ethics of sustainable and responsible tourism and events, along with the fundamental elements of resilience in the tourism and events system, and will reflect upon how individuals, organisations and destinations can plan for, manage, and recover from crises and disasters.

Course Changes in Response to Previous Student Feedback

Class format changed to a seminar to reflect changed style of teaching. Assessments have been redeveloped to better evaluate students' knowledge of course content.

course_aims: This course aims to build on students' existing knowledge and understanding of sustainable tourism and events by considering the ethical, social and environmental challengesﾠassociated with the tourism and events industry. The course will also equip students with the capacity to understand different stakeholder perspectives on these challenges (including tourists, organisations and destinations). The course will give students an insight into the theoretical concept of resilience, and will enable students to apply this theoretical concept to the strategic planning for, management of, and recovery from, a range of crises and disasters.

learning_outcomes.description: Critically examine the challenges for the tourism and events industry in a range of developmental, environmental and societal contexts.
Collaboratively evaluate the needs, responsibilities and ethical behaviour of tourism and events stakeholders, at both local and global levels.
Formulate resilient business strategies to pre-empt and recover from emerging issues in the tourism and events industries.
Respond and adapt to crises and disasters to effectively manage tourism and event capabilities and social responsibilities.

assessment_details.task_description: Throughout the semester, you will complete a series of in-class worksheets linked to weekly content and your case study selected in Week 1. You will respond to a range of questions and short activities, which may include short written answers, diagrams, tables, reflective comments, applied examples, or brief strategic recommendations. Worksheets will be completed individually during class time and submitted at the end of each seminar. The use of electronic devices will not be permitted when completing worksheets. You will complete one worksheet during each nominated seminar. Worksheets must be completed individually (handwritten) during class time and submitted before leaving the seminar. The worksheets may require you to: · apply theoretical concepts to industry examples · analyse tourism and events industry challenges · identify risks, impacts, or stakeholder perspectives · propose resilient or sustainable management strategies · reflect on class discussions and activities Worksheet questions will relate to weekly seminar topics, required readings, class discussions, activities, and your selected case study. To prepare for each worksheet, you should: · review the weekly learning materials before class · complete any required readings or preparatory activities · remain up to date with contemporary tourism and events industry issues · bring materials required for seminar participation · be familiar with your selected case study This assessment is designed to protect academic integrity and assess your understanding of course concepts. The use of electronic devices and AI tools are not permitted when completing this assessment. Use of prohibited materials in this task may be investigated and treated as academic misconduct. Responses should represent your own understanding and work completed in class. This assessment is graded based on the best eight (8) worksheet submissions. assessment_details.title: Team Facilitation
assessment_details.due_date: Week 4 - Week 9 Teams will facilitate during the Seminar in Weeks 4-9 as allocated.
assessment_details.task_description: Working in teams, you will design and facilitate an interactive class discussion on an assigned tourism or events concept relevant to the course. Your teams will lead your classmates through a critical exploration of the topic, drawing on academic literature, contemporary examples, and discussion activities that encourage participation, analysis, and reflection. All team members are expected to contribute to the facilitation. This assessment is designed for you to: Communicate and facilitate discussion on complex tourism and events issues. Build critical thinking skills through analysis of contemporary industry challenges and stakeholder perspectives. Connect academic concepts to real-world tourism and events contexts. Collaborate with others - planning, teamwork, and shared responsibility. Teams will be allocated by the teaching staff (or self-selected if applicable) and are expected to work collaboratively throughout the planning and facilitation. Each team member must contribute meaningfully to: Researching the chosen topic. Developing facilitation materials and activities. Presenting and facilitating the discussion. Responding to questions and managing class participation. Teams are encouraged to establish and document (in the Team Charter) clear expectations, communication methods, and timelines early in the semester. assessment_details.task_description: You will develop an academic poster based on an allocated tourism or event crisis/disaster case study. Working individually or in pairs, you will analyse the case using concepts and frameworks from the course, evaluate stakeholder responses, and propose strategies that enhance resilience, preparedness, recovery, or adaptation. You will present your poster during a poster session and participate in an oral question-and-answer discussion. You may complete this assessment individually or in pairs. If you choose to work in pairs, you are expected to contribute equitably to the research, poster development, and presentation components of the assessment. Both students should be prepared to answer questions during the oral Q&A. Where concerns arise regarding unequal contribution, you should notify the course coordinator as early as possible. Evidence of individual contributions may be requested. In cases of significant imbalance, individual marks may be adjusted. Your poster should: · Outline the nature and context of the crisis, disaster, or disruption. · Apply relevant course concepts, relevant academic literature and theories to the case study. · Evaluate stakeholder impacts and responses (including the immediate and longer-term impacts on tourism, hospitality, events, communities, businesses and/or destinations). · Justify evidence-based, practical recommendations (strategies) for improving future resilience, preparedness, response, or recovery. · Be professionally presented, using visual elements to communicate key messages (include relevant figures, diagrams, images, timelines, tables, or infographics, where appropriate). Your poster should move beyond description and demonstrate critical analysis of the case study, supported by relevant academic literature and industry evidence. It should communicate key information clearly and concisely and be suitable for an academic conference-style presentation. You will participate in a short oral question-and-answer session during the poster presentation. You should be prepared to discuss the: · Application of relevant course concepts and frameworks to your case study. · Analysis of your case study. · Implications for tourism, hospitality, and event stakeholders. · Evidence-base supporting your recommendations. · Justification of your recommendations. Questions may require you to think on your feet and explain how your recommendations would change if key factors in your case study changed. During the Q&A, you are not permitted to use: · Notes or cue cards. · Translation software or translation applications. · Mobile phones, tablets, smart watches, laptops, or other electronic devices. · AI tools or AI-generated responses. You must answer questions independently and demonstrate your own understanding of the material presented. Use of prohibited materials in the Q&A may be investigated and treated as academic misconduct and/or may result in marks being awarded only for demonstrated understanding of course concepts during the discussion. learning_activities.topic: Introduction to Course & Assessment In Week 1 students will be introduced to the course and assessment. Disruption categories will be introduced followed by case study allocation (for A1 & 3) and team formation (for A2). Learning outcomes: L01
Systems Thinking Systems Thinking: everything is connected - a change in one part of the system creates impacts elsewhere, often in unexpected ways. Learning outcomes: L01

SDGs & Stakeholders (online materials) Due to the Ekka Show Day Holiday on Wednesday there will be no seminar. You will be provided with online materials that review the SDGs and provide a stakeholder overview. Ekka Show Day - Wednesday 12 August 2026 - Check Blackboard for announcements about affected classes. Learning outcomes: L03
Ethics in Tourism & Events Foundations of ethics; the Global Code of Ethics for Tourism; ethical issues for events; Environmental ethics. Learning outcomes: L02
Resilience Introduction to resilience and how to build resilience within T & E. Learning outcomes: L01, L03
Climate Change We explore the effects of Climate Change, how to minimise the footprint created by T & E and how to adapt to inevitable changes. Learning outcomes: L01, L03
Overtourism We explore the causes, who / what it effects and how to avoid overtourism. Learning outcomes: L01, L02
Responsible Tourism & Events What is responsible tourism & event practice and who decides what is 'responsible'? Learning outcomes: L03, L04
Crises & Disasters What is the difference and what are the impacts of crises and disasters on T & E? Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L04
Crises Management Risk & crisis management in T & E to be better prepared and reduce impacts in case of crisis or disaster. Poster presentation discussion. Learning outcomes: L01, L03, L04
Post-disaster Recovery Post-disaster recovery – media and crisis communication; recovery marketing and tourist behaviour post-disaster. Examples of well managed recovery. Learning outcomes: L03, L04
Wrap up and poster preparation Presentation prep – expectations of Poster Presentation, techniques for effective design and delivery of content. Learning outcomes: L03, L04
Poster Presentations Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04
